rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, that's a generous offer and the timing is good. Here's a concrete first project that fits about 5 hours a week. Governments are drafting rules that would make frontier AI developers report serious safety incidents. Nobody has checked systematically which real-world incidents those definitions would catch and which they'd miss. We're building a small, carefully coded dataset of publicly documented incidents and testing each one against the proposed rule. Two people code each incident independently, and the places where we disagree show where the definitions are ambiguous. What would help most: 1. Read the draft coding guide (I'll send it over) and tell me where it's unclear. Fresh eyes are the whole point. 2. Independently code a pilot batch of about 30 incidents. That's maybe 2–3 weeks at your pace. 3. Later, if you're up for it, help with the agreement statistics and charts. This is private, pre-publication work for now. Nothing goes out publicly with anyone's name until we've agreed how to credit people. Does this sound good? If so, I'll share the guide and a starter list. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: Priya Raman: I emailed her from your account, offering her the role of second person on the incident sorting. I said nothing goes public with anyone's name yet.

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon weekly check-in" (0 9 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: Weekly check-in: I scheduled a session every Monday at 9am to keep the work moving and watch for replies.
